units.text: AirPods are one of Apple’s most interesting products. The demand for them was largely invented by the fact that the company removed the headphone jack 10 years ago, and now most of us carry this almost magical pair of earbuds that do so much more than just play audio. AirPods offer best-in-class noise cancellation, and also serve as a hearing aid. They get better and better almost every year.
Despite everything that AirPods do so well, I have one annoyance with them, and it’s particularly annoying because it could be such an easy software fix.

Right now, if your AirPods need to charge and you plug your iPhone in, you’ll get a notification to also charge your AirPods. This is because Apple figures that it’d probably be no hassle to charge your AirPods while you’re charging your iPhone, and that reminder has saved me from unknowingly having dead AirPods many times.
AirPods often end up dead in the case

If you’ve owned AirPods for a while, you might be quite familiar with this problem: something got in between the pins of your charging case and one of your AirPods, and you pull them out of the case with one of them dead. This can often ruin your walk, commute, or so on.

At least to me, it seems obvious to add a notification to tell users that one of their AirPods isn’t charging. If one of the AirPods is in the case, and the other isn’t detected in-ear, it’s likely safe to assume it’s in the case but not charging, and Apple could then alert the user to adjust the AirPod or make sure theres no obstruction in the case.
View all comments
It’d be such a simple fix to such a major annoyance, and it’d be yet another instance of Apple magic letting you know that one of your AirPods isn’t charging, before it’s too late.
Hopefully, Apple can implement such a feature in a later iOS update. Right now, the latest-generation AirPods Pro 3 are on sale for $179, in case you don’t own a pair.

units.text: In this week's Sunday Reboot, the expansion of Apple Pay and Apple Music to some countries has taken a decade longer than they really should. They also demonstrate how delays can happen for many different reasons.
Sunday Reboot is a weekly column covering some of the lighter stories within the Apple reality distortion field from the past seven days. All to get next week underway with a good first step.
Apple Music adds to its territory list

It may be a surprise to some readers, but I'm not in the United States. I'm one of the few members of the editorial team based in the United Kingdom, but trained to write in the American way, and forget about the letter U in some words.
This does lead to some issues when it comes to trying out Apple's new services. It's a problem when your whole job is to talk about them.
Thankfully, the UK does have access to almost all of Apple's services, but there are blind spots and differences.

For example, while I have access to Apple Pay, I cannot use services like Apple Card because they are US-only for the moment. Except that I have to change region sometimes for reporting, and now I annoyingly have an Apple Cash card permanently visible in the Wallet app that I cannot use at all.

A little less pressing is the lack of puzzles in News+ over here. Though I can understand the financial problems in setting up Apple Card in the UK, it seems there would be fewer obstacles in adding brainteasers to Apple News, just as U.S. users enjoy.
That said, I am still quite glad to be in the UK where Apple products and services come into play. Partly because we don't suffer from the EU blackout of some upcoming features.
We at least get the updates fairly quickly. Unlike some service updates that happened this week.
Apple Music has expanded into four new countries, including Albania.
On Wednesday, an update to Apple Music finally rolled it out into four countries: Albania, Brunei, Burkina Faso, and Pakistan.
This sounds fairly OK, until you remember that Apple Music was unveiled in June 2015 in over 100 countries. It's taken over 11 years for Apple Music to be available in those four countries.
There's no real explanation for the lack of support in those countries, nor why it took so long.
The more time-consuming problems would revolve around licensing negotiations. However, both Apple and record labels like money, and so you'd expect negotiations to happen at a fairly quick pace.
Then again, it could easily be because Apple has bigger problems at hand than adding support to some countries it's seemingly forgotten about for over a decade.
Regardless, it's a good thing that Apple Music is now available in four more territories that endured a very long wait.

It also reminds me that I'm lucky to live where I do. While there are always going to be differences between US and UK availability for things, I'm not realistically going to be waiting for a decade for anything.
Wait, Apple Pay wasn't in India already?
Slightly less puzzling is the Apple Pay update on the same day. After launching in 2014, Apple finally brought Apple Pay live in India.
It certainly makes sense for Apple to do so, because it is a massive market, and an emerging one at that.
The problem here is that Apple said back in 2017 that it was trying to bring Apple Pay to India. That's a nine-year wait.
As for why it took so long, we could certainly blame regulations for that. In June 2022, more financial laws were introduced, which got in the way.

While in the rest of the world you could use Face ID for a transaction, India instead wanted everyone to use its Aadhaar ID system instead. The laws also covered subscriptions, requiring banks to notify users 24 hours in advance of any recurring transactions, and allowing them to cancel.
Apple Pay is finally available in India.

There's also the matter of a card tokenization framework, which required the use of encrypted tokens issued by local banks in India. This would've required Apple to make changes to how Apple Pay's security and authentication ultimately functioned.
Support for the country's Unified Payments Interface also caused problems.
It was so bad that, in 2022, Apple gave up on credit and debit cards completely in the country.

During this time, both Google Play and Samsung Wallet opted to comply with the law instead of ceasing card payments. It was clearly a case of Apple seeing a massive amount of work and rules that it would have to comply with, and the belief that it could work around or negotiate the hurdles away.
After negotiating with banks to get around the problematic elements, Apple eventually tested card payments in India in July 2026, months before Apple Pay's rollout.
The final introduction of Apple Pay in India is certainly a good thing for Apple, especially in such an important market.

It will be interesting to see how much change Apple Pay will make to iPhone sales in India. It's main rivals have a very large head start because of Apple's unwillingness to abide by the new laws, so it has a lot of catching up to do.
Finally, eventually
Apple's decision to expand the reach of two of its services at the same time demonstrates that there can be a variety of reasons for a delay of a service rolling out in a country.

For Apple Pay in India, as well as the various features EU users cannot access, it's a regulatory problem. When you have to deal with legal issues affecting over a hundred countries simultaneously, you have to prioritize and pick your battles.
Even if it's something that can take years to fully resolve.

For others, like bringing Apple Music to Albania, it seems to be less about legal issues and sticking to the letter of the law. It could just as easily be Apple making it a very low priority for it to work on because there's not enough value to work harder at it.
With Apple Pay in India, there's enough of a carrot for Apple to work to fix it. Even if it does take close to a decade to resolve.

units.text: Since Jony Ive’s departure from Apple in 2019, the company hasn’t had much of a true design lead. For a while, former COO Jeff Williams was in charge of design, until his departure last year. Since then, CEO John Ternus has taken a significant interest in both of Apple’s design teams: industrial design and human interface, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.

This story actually begins prior to John Ternus becoming CEO, which only took place about a month ago. It started with Jeff Williams’ departure as COO. At the time, the company announced that these teams would be reporting to former CEO Tim Cook, but instead, it was reportedly John Ternus. This was one of his key responsibilities while transitioning into CEO.

Of course, it’s no surprise that Ternus is interested in design, seeing as he was formerly in charge of hardware engineering. However, Gurman describes Ternus’ involvement as being “immersed” in the work, and that he often stops by to work with the teams:

Since becoming CEO, however, he has immersed himself in the industrial design and human interface teams. Several people familiar with the department say he works hands-on in the studio several times a week, sometimes visiting multiple times in a single day.
This is in stark contrast to former CEO Tim Cook, who only visited the studio about once a month, per Bloomberg.
Ternus is ‘immersed’ with Apple’s design teams

Ternus as also devoted much attention to refilling the design team’s roles, as the company has lost much talent to outside companies poaching talent. Most notably, Alan Dye left to join Meta, and OpenAI has poached many Apple employees. To rejuvenate the team, Apple has promoted many junior designers and hired new talent from the outside.
View all comments

Throughout all of this, the company still hasn’t sought out a true Jony Ive replacement to serve as a Chief Design Officer of sorts. According to Bloomberg, no search is underway. Instead, the company has highlighted Molly Anderson and Steve Lemay as respective design leads for industrial design and human interface, with Ternus himself serving as the overarching decision maker for design.
While Ternus lacks a traditional design background, his dedication to it means one thing: design will remain a key cornerstone at the top of Apple.

units.text: John Ternus is putting his stamp on Apple by focusing on the company's design work, with the CEO taking an almost Jobsian approach to make design great again.

The era of Tim Cook as Apple CEO was one of growth, with sales and manufacturing the core of his tenure at the top. Under the rule of Ternus, design is becoming a top priority once more for the company, as Ternus aims to add more to the company by strengthening its weaker areas.

Writing in Sunday's "Power On" newsletter for Bloomberg, Mark Gurman writes about a conversation between Ternus and Cook, and how Ternus needed to be himself as CEO instead of emulating Cook. To Ternus, it was an apparent turning point.
Cook had spent his tenure as CEO working on where he could generate "the most value for Apple," Ternus told employees. Therefore, Ternus believed he had to do the same, while still being himself.

The result is that areas Cook focused on, such as financial strategy and the supply chain, are being handled by CFO Kevan Parekh and COO Sabih Khan. Ternus, who is very much an engineer, is instead working closely with chief hardware officer Johny Srouji and hardware engineering leader Tom Marieb.

At the same time, he's also taking a lot more time to look at design, which has fallen behind since the departure of Jony Ive in 2019. There were leaders working for the industrial design and human interface design groups, but they were separate rather than a single executive covering both areas.

Those leaders also reported to former COO Jeff Williams, who had a background in manufacturing but not design. When Williams retired in 2025, those teams were said to be reporting directly to Cook instead.

Instead, there has been an effort by Apple to shore up what it already has and to rebuild. That has included bringing Anderson and Dye successor Steve Lemay to the fore with the launch of the iPhone Duo, as well as hiring more designers for its team.
Apple may not be searching for someone to take control over the design teams right now. Considering the amount of attention for design he has at the moment, Ternus may believe he can do it himself.

units.text: 苹果新任首席执行官John Ternus上任头几周将设计列为优先事项。此外，除了触摸屏和转向OLED技术外，苹果改版后的MacBook Pro还有另一项重大变化。最后，该公司即将发布新的智能家居中枢、HomePod mini和搭载Siri AI的Apple TV。

苹果首席执行官John Ternus将大量时间用于监督公司的硬件和软件设计工作。在早期讨论由John Ternus接替Tim Cook出任苹果首席执行官时，这位较年轻的高管曾质疑自己是否能胜任这一挑战。“我不像你，”Ternus对Cook说。“你做了那么多了不起的事。”Cook以他一贯不动声色的语气回答：“我知道你不像我。”他的意思是，Ternus需要做他自己。Ternus在向员工讲述这段经历时，将其描述为一个转折点。Ternus说，Cook的话“确实引起了我的共鸣，并让我铭记在心”，即他在担任首席执行官期间，把时间花在能为苹果“创造最大价值”的地方。“而我需要把时间花在能为苹果创造最大价值的地方。”他说，这一理念让Ternus得以以不同方式对待这一角色。“我们在时间分配上会有差异，但使命和目标是相同的。”

在担任首席执行官期间，Cook将大部分时间花在运营、销售、财务战略和苹果供应链上。他还经常处理公共政策、隐私问题，以及公司与白宫和世界各国政府的关系。Ternus则是从硬件工程师一路晋升，他正在设定明显不同的优先事项。他基本上将公司的财务运营交给首席财务官Kevan Parekh，将供应链交给首席运营官Sabih Khan。相反，Ternus花大量时间与首席硬件官Johny Srouji和硬件工程负责人Tom Marieb在一起，深入参与产品工程。但我获悉，他还将大量精力投入到另一个长期缺乏单一最高负责人的领域：设计。

自Jony Ive于2019年离职以来，苹果一直缺乏一位统一负责工业设计——即硬件的外观和质感——以及人机界面设计——即塑造公司软件的设计——的设计主管。在随后的几年里，工业设计和人机界面设计各有负责人，而不是由一位高管统一管理这两个团队。他们最终向时任首席运营官Jeff Williams汇报。Williams是一位没有设计背景的制造专家，他之所以被选中负责该部门，很大程度上是因为他与Cook关系密切。当Williams去年退休时，这一安排发生了变化。尽管Cook在新闻稿中宣布，Williams离职后设计团队将直接向他汇报——表面上的确如此——但实际上他们开始向Ternus汇报。作为最终过渡到首席执行官的一部分，Cook将设计职责交给了他。在4月至9月的首席执行官过渡期间，苹果的设计负责人实际上是Ternus在Cook卸任前唯一的直接下属。

作为苹果硬件工程负责人，Ternus已经在一定程度上参与了设计工作室的工作，因为这两个职能需要密切协调。然而，自担任首席执行官以来，他已深入参与工业设计和人机界面团队。几位熟悉该部门的人士称，他每周都会多次亲临工作室，有时一天会去好几次。当然，Steve Jobs在与Ive合作期间也以类似方式直接参与设计。但Ternus的参与标志着与Cook时代的重大转变。设计师们称，Cook通常每月最多去工作室一次，每次约一小时。

Ternus的首要任务之一是恢复设计工作室在公司内部的地位。该团队曾有大量员工流失，去了Ive的公司LoveFrom，以及OpenAI的硬件团队和其他公司。这导致其在苹果内部的影响力和可信度下降。人员流失迫使公司提拔初级设计师，并从外部大量招聘以补充团队。苹果长期负责软件设计的Alan Dye跳槽去了Meta Platforms Inc．。Ive的工业设计主管继任者Evans Hankey也离开了，最终加入了OpenAI。Hankey后来由Molly Anderson接替，Anderson在更广泛的设计界知名度较低，在2024年成为工业设计副总裁之前，从未在苹果管理过如此规模的团队。到那时，该团队许多最资深的成员已经离开，缩小了苹果内部候选人的范围，使Anderson成为唯一现实的内部人选。

units.text: IT之家 10 月 4 日消息，博主 @数码闲聊站 今日爆料，苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 系列 W39 周累计销量 176 万台（预计指国内），根据国庆期间的走势，W40 预估累计销量超 250 万台，两款机型均轻松完成单品激活 100 万台。
IT之家注意到，W39 指的是 2026 年的第 39 个自然周，也就是 9 月 21 日到 9 月 27 日这一周。手机行业习惯用“W+ 周数”来标记周次，方便对比每周的销量和市场份额变化。
苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 与 iPhone 18 Pro Max 两款机型于 9 月 18 日正式开售，国行起售价为 9999 元，均为 256GB 存储起步。
两款机型均搭载全新 A20 Pro 芯片，采用台积电 2nm 制程工艺，其 CPU 与 GPU 性能较上一代显著提升，端侧 AI 性能进一步增强。同时，iPhone 18 Pro 系列配备新一代均热板散热方案，苹果官方称其带来“iPhone 历来最出色持续效能表现”。
影像系统是此次升级的核心。iPhone 18 Pro 系列配备 4800 万像素融合式主摄，首次引入可变光圈技术，内部采用六片激光切割叶片，支持 f/1.48、f/1.8、f/2.8 和 f/4.0 四档光圈调节。用户可在相机应用中手动调整光圈设置，开发者也可通过 API 在第三方应用中调用光圈控制功能。
iPhone 18 Pro Max 的电池续航提升幅度为 iPhone 历代之最，官网标称可提供最长 29~43 小时的续航时间。同时，iPhone 18 Pro Max 的充电速度也实现了大幅跃升，在搭配 60W 及以上 AVS 电源适配器（另售）的情况下可以在约 15 分钟时间内充至最大 50% 电量，实测峰值功率达 52W。

units.text: Apple’s major MacBook Pro overhaul is just around the corner, and should debut within a month or so. It’ll be the first touchscreen MacBook, as well as the first with Tandem OLED. Beyond that, though, the new MacBooks should be ‘significantly’ lighter than their predecessors, according to the latest issue of the Power On newsletter.

The newsletter reiterates that the new MacBook Pro should debut ‘by next month,’ so we should see these new machines before the end of November. These machines should offer the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, as Apple has opted to skip the higher-end part of the M6 family in favor of accelerating the M7 launch.
New MacBook Pro to be much lighter

Despite the fact that these MacBooks have been rumored for quite some time, we haven’t really known too much about them besides specs on paper: OLED, touch, Dynamic Island, and so on. In the past, reports have described the computer as thinner, but we haven’t really had much of a visual. We still don’t, but we do have one major new detail on what this machine will feel like:

The new MacBook Pros are lighter — significantly lighter. Apple has reengineered the machine’s interior miniaturizing parts and rearranging components to make the computer much easier to carry. The current 16-inch MacBook Pro weighs as much as 4.8 pounds, compared with 3.3 pounds for the 15-inch MacBook Air, so any meaningful reduction would be immediately noticeable.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman doesn’t specify exactly how much lighter it will be, but if you’re someone who uses a current-generation MacBook Pro, especially the 16-inch, you might find that it’s heavier than you’d like it to be. Apple is reportedly working to improve on that.

units.text: The forthcoming new MacBook Pro is expected to bring an OLED touch-screen, but it's also now predicted to be at least a little closer to the MacBook Air's lower weight.

Every detail of the expected MacBook Pro refresh has been rumored, sometimes for years, as Apple hasn't made even a minor design change since 2022. That includes the expectation that the new MacBook Pro will be lighter, which was first reported back in 2024.
However, Bloomberg now claims that the weight difference will be significant. Reportedly, Apple has redesigned components, making them smaller and so lighter.

It's also claimed that the positioning of some components have been rearranged to make the MacBook Pro easier to carry. That's harder to imagine as the MacBook Pro is already built so that its weight is evenly distributed.

Nonetheless, any significant reduction in weight is going to be a selling point. It's not as if Apple will talk up the lightness before it does a hard sell on the OLED touchscreen, but it is important.

That won't be the case for people who chiefly leave their MacBook Pro on a desk. But if you've ever switched between a MacBook Pro and a MacBook Air, you have noticed the substantial weight difference.
The current 16-inch MacBook Pro weighs 4.7 pounds while the nearest equivalent, the 15-inch MacBook Air, is 3.3 pounds.
Apple is now expected to launch the revised MacBook Pro in either late October 2026 or November 2026. That will make it just in time to still be in the MacBook Pro's 20th anniversary year.

units.text: 彭博社记者马克·古尔曼称，苹果正在重新设计下一代MacBook Pro的内部结构，通过缩小部分组件并调整组件布局，使新机“明显更轻”，携带起来也更方便。不过，报道没有给出具体减重幅度，也未说明14英寸和16英寸机型是否会采用相同方案。苹果尚未公布这款产品，相关信息仍属媒体报道和传闻。
这款重新设计的MacBook Pro预计将配备OLED触控屏。此前有关产品的报道还提及更薄机身，以及可能以灵动岛取代现款屏幕刘海；彭博社称新机或于今年10月或11月推出。上述设计和发布时间均未获苹果官方确认，苹果也未说明触控屏型号的最终产品名称、处理器配置或重量。

减重对大尺寸机型尤其有意义。苹果现售16英寸MacBook Pro搭载M5 Pro或M5 Max芯片，机重约2.14至2.15公斤；作为参照，15英寸MacBook Air约重1.5公斤。古尔曼没有披露新机最终重量，因此目前无法判断它能缩小多少与MacBook Air之间的差距。AppleInsider指出，MacBook Pro自2022年以来没有进行明显的外观改款，轻量化传闻此前已出现，但这次关于“显著减重”的说法来自古尔曼最新报道。
如果传闻属实，这将是苹果首次推出触控屏MacBook Pro，并在增加触控功能的同时降低整机重量。不过目前仍没有具体尺寸、厚度、屏幕参数、重量或价格等官方数据，实际改动幅度仍有待苹果发布时确认。

如果传闻属实，这将是苹果首次推出触控屏MacBook Pro，并在增加触控功能的同时降低整机重量。不过目前仍没有具体尺寸、厚度、屏幕参数、重量或价格等官方数据，实际改动幅度仍有待苹果发布时确认。

units.text: 快科技10月5日消息，据报道，苹果将会在11月底之前推出经过深度重新设计的MacBook Pro，这一代机型将迎来多项历史性的变化，不管是屏幕交互还是机身便携性，都有不小升级。
这是Mac系列历史上第一款支持触控操作的MacBook，同时首次用上叠层OLED屏幕，屏幕区域还会搭载灵动岛设计。
长久以来，Mac电脑一直没有触屏功能，这次更新补齐了这一大短板，打通了和iPad之间的交互体验壁垒。
硬件核心方面，新款机型沿用M5 Pro与M5 Max芯片，苹果选择跳过M6系列高端版本，以此加速后续M7芯片的研发落地。
除屏幕之外，本次更新的一大惊喜是机身重量的明显下降。苹果对内部架构进行重新规划，把零部件小型化，调整元器件排布，实现了显著减重。
目前16英寸MacBook Pro重量约2.2千克，不少用户反馈日常外出携带负担较重，虽然爆料没有公布确切减重数字，但表示上手就可以感受到重量差异，大幅改善Pro机型的便携短板。
软件层面，macOS 27.2正式版会配套上线，针对触控操作、灵动岛完成系统适配，为新硬件提供完整的软件支持。
目前还没有真机外观的实拍信息，但是综合多方消息，这款新机属于近几年MacBook Pro改动幅度最大的一代产品。
